name: Finland
traditionNote: A Nordic civil-law system: the starting point is the enacted statute text in Finlex, read together with its travaux préparatoires (the hallituksen esitys and committee reports), while Supreme Court and Supreme Administrative Court ennakkopäätökset guide interpretation without formally binding later courts.
summary: Acts (laki / lag) are passed by the unicameral Eduskunta, confirmed by the President of the Republic, and given force by publication in the Suomen säädöskokoelma — the Statute Book of Finland. Decrees (asetus / förordning) are issued by the Government, the President or individual ministries under an authorisation in an act, and are published in the same series; more detailed regulations of state agencies appear in the ministries' and authorities' määräyskokoelmat. Since 1 January 2011 the Statute Book has been published electronically in Finlex as its primary form, the printed edition having been discontinued; each statute appears both as text and as a PDF facsimile laid out like the old printed sheet. A statute enters into force on the date it names, and if it names none, on publication. Finland is bilingual: statutes are enacted and published in Finnish and in Swedish, and both language versions are equally authentic — there is no 'original' and 'translation' between them.
hierarchy: Suomen perustuslaki / Finlands grundlag (Constitution, 731/1999) and constitutional-order acts such as the Åland Self-Government Act
EU law (directly applicable regulations; treaties brought into force by an act of Parliament, the voimaansaattamislaki)
Laki / Lag — acts of the Eduskunta
Tasavallan presidentin, valtioneuvoston ja ministeriön asetus — decrees of the President, Government and ministries
Viranomaisten määräykset ja ohjeet — binding regulations and guidance of state agencies, published in the määräyskokoelmat
Kunnalliset säännöt, taksat ja johtosäännöt — municipal by-laws and charters adopted under the Local Government Act
Ålands landskapslagar och landskapsförordningar — parallel, not subordinate, within Åland's legislative competence

gazette.name: Suomen saadoskokoelma
gazette.authority: Oikeusministeriö (Ministry of Justice); published by Oikeusrekisterikeskus (Legal Register Centre) in Finlex
gazette.coverage: Year index runs from 1734 (the Swedish Code) and 1868 onward, then continuously through the twentieth century to the current year; electronic publication is the primary form since 1 January 2011
gazette.desc: The series in which acts, decrees and other statutes are published and thereby given legal force. Each item carries a number/year citation (e.g. 731/1999) and is offered both as running text and as a PDF facsimile matching the layout of the former printed Statute Book. This is the as-enacted record, distinct from the consolidated texts elsewhere on Finlex.
gazette.howto: Browse the year list, or use the 'Siirry säädökseen (numero/vuosi)' box to jump straight to a citation — type 731 and 1999 for the Constitution. The ten most recently published statutes are listed on the landing page under 'Uusimmat säädökset säädöskokoelmassa'; the Swedish text is reached through the language switch in the page header.
gazette.note: Finlex was rebuilt on a new URL scheme in 2025. Most legacy deep links of the finlex.fi/fi/laki/... form now redirect to their new addresses — /fi/laki/ajantasa/1999/19990731 lands on /fi/lainsaadanto/1999/731 — but the old translation URLs (/fi/laki/kaannokset/...) return 404.

constitution.name: Suomen perustuslaki 731/1999
constitution.coverage: Adopted 11 June 1999, in force since 1 March 2000; consolidated with all subsequent amendments
constitution.desc: The single consolidated constitutional instrument that in 2000 replaced Finland's four older constitutional acts. Finlex shows the up-to-date text with amendments incorporated; the Swedish text at finlex.fi/sv/lagstiftning/1999/731 is Finlands grundlag and is equally authentic.
constitution.howto: Open the page and read the consolidated text section by section; switch to /sv/ for the Swedish version. The translations listed on this statute are English, German, French, Spanish and Russian — there is no Japanese text of the Constitution — and each sits at /fi/lainsaadanto/saadoskaannokset/1999/{eng|deu|fra|spa|rus}/731. The as-enacted 1999 text with its PDF facsimile sits under the Statute Book at finlex.fi/en/legislation/collection/1999/731.
constitution.note: Constitutional amendments are made through the ordinary legislative procedure in an aggravated form; there is no separate constitutional court, and review is exercised chiefly ex ante by Parliament's Constitutional Law Committee.

sources.name: Ajantasainen lainsaadanto (Finlex)
sources.authority: Oikeusrekisterikeskus (Legal Register Centre), for the Ministry of Justice
sources.coverage: Statutes in force, with amendments incorporated; tracked to the most recent published statute number
sources.desc: The version practitioners actually read: the text of an act or decree with every later amendment merged in. This is where you go for 'what does the law say today', as opposed to the Statute Book, which shows what was published on a given day in a given year.
sources.howto: Search by name or keyword, or enter a number/year citation directly. Each statute page lists the amending statutes, their entry-into-force dates, and links across to the original Statute Book item, the Swedish text and any translations.
sources.note: Consolidation is editorial work performed on top of the published statutes; where precision matters the as-published Statute Book item is the record.

sources.name: Saadoskaannokset (Finlex)
sources.authority: Oikeusministeriö / Oikeusrekisterikeskus, compiling translations produced by ministries
sources.coverage: Several hundred acts, unevenly across subject areas; each translation states the amendment number it is updated to
sources.desc: The nearest thing to an English text of Finnish law, gathered in one place and labelled by the site itself as 'unofficial translations of statutes into foreign languages'. Coverage is selective — major codes and business-facing acts are translated, much else is not.
sources.howto: Browse alphabetically or by year, or open any statute in Finlex and take the 'Translations' tab. Check the header of the translation for the statute number it has been updated through; the English Constitution, for example, is revised to 817/2018.
sources.note: No translation is authentic. Only the Finnish and Swedish texts have legal force, and a translation may lag years behind the current consolidated text.

sources.name: Saamenkieliset saadokset (Finlex)
sources.coverage: Translations from 1991 onward, in Northern Sámi (sme), Inari Sámi (smn) and Skolt Sámi (sms)
sources.desc: Statutes translated into the three Sámi languages spoken in Finland, mainly those bearing on Sámi language rights, the Sámi Homeland and reindeer husbandry. A small collection, but the only organised one of its kind.
sources.howto: Browse the year list, or use the 'Go to statute (number/year)' box to jump to a citation; each entry is tagged with its Sámi language code. There is no alphabetical index here — for that, start from the statute's Finnish page in the consolidated legislation.
sources.note: Sámi versions are translations, not enacted language versions; the Finnish and Swedish texts govern.

sources.name: Oikeuskaytanto (Finlex)
sources.authority: Oikeusrekisterikeskus, publishing decisions supplied by the courts
sources.coverage: Supreme Court precedents from 1926, plus its other decisions and granted leaves to appeal; Supreme Administrative Court precedents, other published decisions and the archive of short summaries; administrative courts from 1981; courts of appeal full text from 2004 (summaries earlier); Market Court from 1979; Labour Court from 1970; Insurance Court from 1961; case law in legal literature from 1926
sources.desc: The single free national case-law database, covering the two supreme courts and the specialist and appellate courts in one search. Decisions are in Finnish or Swedish; there is no comprehensive English case-law collection anywhere.
sources.howto: Use the search box at the top of the section — Perushaku (basic), Etäisyyshaku (proximity) or Laajennettu haku (expanded) — or pick a court from the list on the landing page and browse its years. Citation form resolves directly in the URL: /fi/oikeuskaytanto/korkein-oikeus/ennakkopaatokset/2025/102 is KKO:2025:102 and the same pattern under korkein-hallinto-oikeus gives KHO:2024:1. The 'Oikeuskäytäntö kirjallisuudessa' index points from a decision to the articles discussing it.
sources.note: Only published precedents and selected decisions appear; the bulk of first-instance judgments are not online and must be requested from the court registry.

sources.name: Korkein oikeus
sources.coverage: English summaries of selected precedents from 2017 onward; the full Finnish and Swedish precedent series lives in Finlex
sources.desc: The final instance in civil, commercial and criminal matters, and the body whose ennakkopäätökset steer interpretation of the general courts. This page is the court's own English window, chosen around EU law, human rights and other internationally relevant questions.
sources.howto: Pick a year from the 2017-2026 tabs and scroll the list of English summaries, each headed by its KKO:year:number citation. For the complete precedent series go to korkeinoikeus.fi/ennakkopaatokset/ in Finnish; EU-law and human-rights precedents down to 2015 were published in Swedish instead, under 'Avgöranden med anknytning till EU-rätten och mänskliga rättigheter'.
sources.note: The English items are unofficial summaries prepared by the court, not translations of the judgments. The site itself is also offered in Northern Sámi and French.

sources.name: Korkein hallinto-oikeus
sources.coverage: Decisions from 2024 onward on the court's own site; older published decisions in Finlex
sources.desc: The highest court for administrative matters — taxation, planning, immigration, environment, public procurement, access to documents. Finland's two supreme courts are separate and neither reviews the other, so administrative questions end here rather than at the Korkein oikeus.
sources.howto: Take 'Precedents' for the yearbook (vuosikirja) decisions and 'Other published decisions' for the rest; recent full texts are on this site in Finnish or Swedish, and anything older is retrieved through the Finlex case-law search.
sources.note: English content is limited to summaries of selected precedents; the decisions themselves are not translated.

sources.name: Viranomaisten maarayskokoelmat (Finlex)
sources.authority: Individual ministries and central agencies, aggregated by Oikeusrekisterikeskus
sources.coverage: Ministry decrees and the regulations, instructions, decisions and communications of central government authorities; plus decisions of the Chancellor of Justice, of the Data Protection Ombudsman, and generally applicable collective agreements
sources.desc: Where the detailed rule usually is. A great deal of operative Finnish law sits below the level of a decree — agency määräykset on aviation, finance, food, radiation, transport — and this is the aggregated entry point to those collections.
sources.howto: The landing page splits into four branches: Collections of regulations, Chancellor of Justice, Data Protection Ombudsman and Collective agreements. Take 'Collections of regulations' (/en/authorities/regulations) to reach the list of issuing bodies — Ministry for Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Finnish Food Authority, Finnish Patent and Registration Office, National Police Board and the rest — then browse or search within one collection.
sources.note: Some agencies also publish their regulations on their own sites, occasionally in a more current form than the Finlex copy.

sources.name: Sopimussarja (Finlex)
sources.en: Treaty Series of the Statute Book
sources.coverage: Electronic treaty series from 1999 onward — treaty texts, bringing-into-force acts and decrees, ministry announcements — alongside consolidated income-tax treaties and the treaty reference database (valtiosopimusten viitetietokanta)
sources.desc: Treaties do not take internal effect in Finland by ratification alone — an act or decree brings them into force, and both the treaty text and that instrument are published here with their own SopS number.
sources.howto: Use the section search (Perushaku / Etäisyyshaku / Laajennettu haku) by SopS number/year or by treaty name; each entry pairs the treaty text with the voimaansaattamissäädös that gave it domestic force and with the announcement fixing the date of entry into force. Two sibling collections sit in the same section: 'Ajantasaiset tuloverosopimukset' for consolidated tax treaties and the reference database for basic particulars of every treaty.

sources.name: Hallituksen esitykset (Finlex)
sources.authority: Valtioneuvosto (Government); published in Finlex by Oikeusrekisterikeskus
sources.coverage: 1992-present, in Finnish and Swedish, as text and PDF; plus a list of bills currently pending before Parliament
sources.desc: The hallituksen esitys is the central travaux préparatoire in Finnish legal method — its detailed section-by-section reasoning is routinely relied on to read an ambiguous provision, more so than in common-law systems.
sources.howto: Search by HE number/year, by keyword or by the ministry that prepared the bill; open a statute in Finlex and its preparatory documents are cross-linked from the statute page.
sources.note: Committee reports and plenary records that follow the bill are on the Parliament side, not here.

sources.name: Eduskunta — asiat ja aanestykset
sources.native: Eduskunta — asiat ja äänestykset / Riksdagen — ärenden och omröstningar
sources.en: Parliament of Finland — matters and votes
sources.coverage: Processing records and documents for matters from 2015 onward in the current search; older parliamentary documents 1907-2000 and 1980-onward series through the Parliament's document services
sources.desc: Where a bill is tracked through its stages: committee reports (valiokunnan mietintö), statements of the Constitutional Law Committee, plenary minutes and division results. The Constitutional Law Committee's lausunnot are the closest Finnish equivalent to constitutional case law and are found here.
sources.howto: From this page take 'Valtiopäiväasiat' for matters before the House, 'Käsittelyssä olevat asiat' for what is pending and 'Uusimmat äänestykset' for division results; searching a matter by its HE number opens the käsittelytiedot page listing every document in the file and the date of each reading. The general search at eduskunta.fi/haku spans documents, records and press material.
sources.note: The site returns 403 to automated fetchers and is a JavaScript application, so open it in a browser; scriptable access is the avoindata.eduskunta.fi REST API, whose tables include VaskiData (documents), SaliDB* (plenary and votes) and MemberOfParliament.

sources.name: Finlex avoin data
sources.coverage: Statutes, case law and related materials as structured documents; REST API updated close to real time, bulk packages refreshed daily
sources.desc: Finland publishes its legal corpus in Akoma Ntoso XML, which is unusual and makes bulk reuse genuinely practical — the whole Statute Book and case-law series can be pulled rather than scraped.
sources.howto: Read the quick integration guide, then use the Swagger console at opendata.finlex.fi to build queries; whole-corpus archives are downloadable from the 'download materials' page in the same section.

sources.name: Virallinen lehti
sources.authority: Virallinen lehti Kustannus Oy, publishing under a statutory mandate to carry the notices that law or decree requires to appear in the Virallinen lehti
sources.coverage: Finland's oldest paper still appearing — its bicentenary was marked on 2 November 2019; since the beginning of 2019 it has been electronic-only, twice weekly on Tuesdays and Fridays. The online issue archive runs from 1997 to the current year
sources.desc: Finland's notice gazette, distinct from the Statute Book: bankruptcy and restructuring notices, public summonses, corporate and estate announcements, and other publications the law requires to be made in the Virallinen lehti. Statutes are not published here.
sources.howto: Take 'Sähköinen lehti' to the Julkaistut lehdet listing, pick a year from 1997 onward and open an issue as a PDF laid out like the printed paper; the Haku box searches the published issues. Reading is free — only submitting a notice needs a login, and that is a paid service with a Friday/Wednesday noon deadline for the Tuesday/Friday issues.
sources.note: Do not confuse it with the Suomen säädöskokoelma — a statute takes effect through the säädöskokoelma, not through this journal.

sources.name: Alands forfattningssamling (AFS)
sources.coverage: 1923-present; about 6,650 ÅFS items indexed in the site's own search. Statutes from 1923 to 1997 are scans of the printed edition, so they can be found by year, number and title but their text is not full-text searchable
sources.desc: The official statute series of the autonomous Åland Islands, where the Lagting legislates independently in the areas assigned to it by the Self-Government Act. It carries landskapslagar, landskapsförordningar, Lagting and landskapsregering decisions, presidential decrees concerning Åland, and treaty consents.
sources.howto: Browse the chronological PDF list, newest first, where ÅFS 2024:12 (year:number) denotes a new instrument and ÅFS 2024/12 (year/number) an amendment to an existing one; the year register and its corrections are filed as ÅFS XXXX:0. The search page at regeringen.ax/alandsk-lagstiftning/sok queries ÅFS, Ålex, Ålands lagsamling and the EU-rättelseblad at once, and the 'Gå till författning' box jumps to a citation when you give both year and number.
sources.note: Published in Swedish only — Åland is monolingually Swedish, so there is no Finnish text of an Åland statute. The landskapsregering states that complete and correct knowledge of an ÅFS statute is obtained only from ÅFS in paper form, which is still sold and can be subscribed to.

sources.name: Alex — Alands konsoliderade lagstiftning
sources.coverage: About 690 consolidated Åland statutes in force, organised by subject area, each closing with entry-into-force notes, preparatory references and where relevant the EU legislation concerned; the collection states the ÅFS number it is updated through (ÅFS 2026/46, published 25 June 2026, at the time of checking)
sources.desc: The Åland counterpart of Finlex's consolidated legislation: statute texts with amendments merged in, arranged by topic — Självstyrelsens grunder, Lagtinget, landskapsförvaltningen, health and social care, infrastructure and traffic, agriculture and fishing, taxes, education and culture.
sources.howto: Pick a subject heading from the Ämne list, or go directly by citation — the Självstyrelselag (1991:71) is at /alandsk-lagstiftning/alex/199171 and the Lagtingsordning (2011:97) at /alandsk-lagstiftning/alex/201197, the number being year plus number run together.
sources.note: Ålex states plainly that it may contain errors and that the only way to complete and correct knowledge of a statute is ÅFS in paper form; treat it as a finding aid, not the record.

sources.name: EUR-Lex (suomeksi)
sources.authority: Euroopan unionin julkaisutoimisto (Publications Office of the European Union)
sources.coverage: EU treaties, legislation, consolidated texts, case law, national implementing measures and the Official Journal, in all EU languages including Finnish and Swedish
sources.desc: A large part of the law applied in Finland is EU law: regulations apply directly without a Finnish statute, and directives are traceable to the Finnish acts that implement them. Finlex will not show you a regulation, so this is the second half of the map.
sources.howto: Search by CELEX number or subject with the interface set to Finnish; the 'kansalliset täytäntöönpanotoimenpiteet' tab on a directive lists the Finnish statutes notified as implementing it.
sources.note: The Finnish-language version of an EU act is authentic alongside the other language versions, but the site distinguishes the legally binding Official Journal edition from ordinary display copies.

sources.name: Edilex
sources.authority: Edita Publishing Oy, a private commercial publisher
sources.coverage: Legislation and preparatory materials, court decisions including unpublished ones, legal journals, commentary and a digital book collection; most of it behind a subscription
sources.desc: The service Finnish practitioners actually work in. It layers annotation, news, commentary and unpublished case law over the same statute corpus Finlex gives away, which is precisely why it is worth naming even though it is neither official nor free.
sources.howto: Search legislation, case law or literature from the top bar; the book and journal collections sit in their own sections. Most substantive content requires a subscription.
sources.note: Private and commercial. Nothing here is an official text — for the authentic wording of a statute, go back to Finlex. The site refuses connections from some networks, including automated fetchers, so it may look unreachable when it is not.

findLaw.task: Find the current text of an act in force
findLaw.steps: Search the act's name or its number/year citation in Finlex's consolidated legislation and open the statute page, which shows the text with all amendments merged in. The Swedish text of the same act is one click away and is equally authentic.

findLaw.task: See the statute exactly as it was published (as-enacted)
findLaw.steps: Go to the Statute Book and enter the citation in the 'Siirry säädökseen (numero/vuosi)' box — 731 and 1999 for the Constitution. Each item gives the running text on the page with the säädöskokoelma PDF linked from the reference details above it, in the layout of the old printed Statute Book, which is the record of what was actually published.

findLaw.task: Work out what changed and when it takes effect
findLaw.steps: Open the amendments section, which lists amending statutes with their entry-into-force and repeal dates by year; alternatively the amendment table on any consolidated statute page names every amending act. For the reasoning behind a change, follow the linked hallituksen esitys.

Search the Finlex case-law database by keyword, or go straight to a citation through the court's own branch — KKO:2025:102 resolves at /fi/oikeuskaytanto/korkein-oikeus/ennakkopaatokset/2025/102 and KHO:2024:1 at the matching path under korkein-hallinto-oikeus. Precedents and other published decisions from 2024 onward on the administrative side are also on kho.fi, and English summaries of selected Supreme Court precedents from 2017 onward are on korkeinoikeus.fi.

findLaw.task: Find a decree or an agency regulation, not an act
findLaw.steps: Government and ministry decrees are in the Statute Book alongside acts, under their own number/year. Regulations and binding guidance issued by state agencies are one level down, in the määräyskokoelmat aggregated in Finlex's Authorities section — open 'Collections of regulations', pick the issuing authority from the list, then browse or search its collection.

Use the Åland legislation search on the landskapsregering site to find landskapslagar and landskapsförordningar by keyword, filtering by type (ÅFS, Ålex, Ålands lagsamling, EU-rättelseblad), or use 'Gå till författning' with both year and number. Read the consolidated version in Ålex, then confirm the wording against the ÅFS PDF — note that 1923-1997 statutes are scans, so their text is not searchable. Everything is in Swedish.

findLaw.task: Read a Finnish act in English
findLaw.steps: Check the translations section, browsing alphabetically or by year, and note the amendment number the translation is updated through before relying on it. If no translation exists — which is common — the Finnish or Swedish text on Finlex is the only version there is.

subnational: Finland is a unitary state, and its 300-odd municipalities and the wellbeing services counties do not legislate: they adopt by-laws, charters and tariffs under powers granted by acts of Parliament, and these are published by each municipality itself rather than in any national series. The real exception is Åland, an autonomous Swedish-speaking region whose Lagting enacts landskapslagar with the force of law in the fields assigned to it by the Self-Government Act, published in Ålands författningssamling and consolidated in Ålex, entirely in Swedish. Nothing of Åland's own legislation appears in Finlex beyond a signpost link, so the regeringen.ax site is the only route to it. Sámi self-government through the Saamelaiskäräjät is administrative and consultative, not legislative.
caveats: The consolidated texts on Finlex are editorial compilations maintained on top of the published statutes; where the exact wording matters, the Statute Book item and its PDF facsimile are the record of what was published. Finnish and Swedish are both authentic languages of enactment — a divergence between them is a question of interpretation, not a translation error — while every foreign-language version, including the English Constitution, is expressly unofficial, selectively available and often years behind the current text. Not every statute is translated even into English — the Constitution has English, German, French, Spanish and Russian versions but no Japanese one — so absence of a translation is the normal case, not an oversight. Åland's Ålex warns on its own pages that it may contain errors and that the only way to complete and correct knowledge of a statute is ÅFS in paper form. Finlex was rebuilt on a new URL scheme in 2025; most legacy finlex.fi/fi/laki/... deep links now redirect to the new addresses, but the old translation URLs do not and return 404. Edilex is a private commercial publisher, not an official source, and most of its content sits behind a subscription; the Virallinen lehti, despite the name, is a notice gazette and never the place a statute acquires force.
